info.title: HydroAssist
info.summary: Pumping test analysis that explains itself.
info.description: The calculators, the project model and the consultant, over HTTP. Sessions are per visitor: a conversation is never shared.

get.description: The caller's workspace, created on first contact.
Only the test types that have an implemented method.

schema.title: Response List Test Types Api Test Types Get

get.description:
The methods for a test type, as the registry declares them.

The browser builds its form from this — including which extra inputs a
method needs — so a new method needs no frontend change.

post.description:
Discard the open project. Anything not downloaded is lost, which the UI
warns about before calling this.

get.description: The project as the file the user keeps — this is the only persistence.

post.description:
Inspect, format, diagnose and validate uploaded readings, and record them
against the test.

CSV, tab- or space-delimited text, and Excel workbooks; `table_reader`
chooses by extension.

get.description:
The readings already held by a test — typically a reopened project.

`rows` is how much of the table to return. The default is a preview; the
workspace asks for the whole table when the user opens it to check what was
read, which is the only way to tell a misread column from a correct one.

post.description:
The same intake, for columns pasted from a spreadsheet.

Most people have the numbers open in Excel already, and saving a file first
to upload it is a step that earns nothing. The text goes through the same
reader — the delimiter is sniffed — so a pasted table and an uploaded one
cannot diverge.

Propose a grid from a photograph of a field sheet. Stores nothing.

Deliberately not an intake route. It does not touch `test.readings`, does not
inspect or validate, and does not reach the chat: it hands back what OCR
saw, cell by cell, with the confidence of each. The user corrects the grid
and sends it as text, so an image reaches a calculator only through a person.

A misread digit does not fail — it fits, and reports a wrong transmissivity
with no warning anywhere. That is the whole reason this route is separate.

put.description:
Store the Step 2 form against the test, so saving the project captures
what is on screen.

post.description:
Fit the chosen method to the active test's readings.

The setup is stored on the test first, so the analysis, the project and the
form all describe the same test afterwards.

get.description: The last result, for a browser that reloaded mid-session.

Every fit run in this session, oldest first.

Saving an analysis to the project is a deliberate act, so a fit that was run
and not saved used to leave no trace at all — the next one overwrote it. This
is what was run, which is a different question from what was kept.

schema.title: Response Analysis History Api Analyses History Get

post.description:
The hand-matched curve for the sliders. Every parameter other than T and
S stays at its fitted value; a method that estimates no S ignores it.

Record the last result against the active test, so methods can be
compared rather than recomputed.

get.description:
Saved analyses ranked by AICc — never by R², which cannot penalise an
extra parameter. Analyses run on replaced readings are left out.

The client deliverable: the fit, its figure, its validity notes and the
project metadata.

post.description:
Ask the consultant. The reply lands in the message list, so the browser
redraws from one response.

Rate-limited per session and per day, to stay inside the model's free tier.

Accept the suggested method, or override it. This is the bridge: the
workspace form follows what the conversation settles on.

Start the conversation again. The project and its readings are kept —
only the discussion is cleared.

get.description: The conversation as a plain-text transcript.

post.description:
The same turn as POST /messages, with the answer sent as it is written.

An answer takes several seconds, and the first sentence of an interpretation
usually says whether the fit can be trusted. There is no reason to withhold it
until the last sentence exists.

Server-sent events, three kinds:

    {"type": "token", "text": "…"}    a piece of the answer
    {"type": "state", ...}            the whole chat state, once, at the end
    {"type": "error", "detail": "…"}  the turn failed; replace the partial text

The turn runs in a worker thread and pushes tokens into a queue that this
response drains — the alternative, generating inside the request, cannot yield
anything until the model has finished, which is the problem being solved.

What is *stored* is identical to the non-streaming route, so a reload shows
the same conversation either way, and the browser can fall back to
POST /messages whenever streaming is unavailable.

ActionModel.title: ActionModel
ActionModel.description:
Somewhere the guide offered to take the user.

An offer, never a move: the browser renders a button and nothing happens
until it is pressed. An assistant that navigates the workspace by itself
while someone is mid-analysis is a worse failure than one that answers
badly.

AnalysisRunModel.title: AnalysisRunModel
AnalysisRunModel.description:
One fit run in this session, saved or not.

The workspace keeps saved analyses in the project, but a fit that was run and
not saved existed nowhere: it vanished when the next one replaced it, which is
how three analyses in a row came to look like one. This is the log of what was
actually run.

DiagnosisModel.title: DiagnosisModel
DiagnosisModel.description: What the Bourdet derivative says the flow regime is.

gated_out.title: Gated Out
gated_out.description: Methods the validator does not offer for this dataset

gated_reasons.title: Gated Reasons
gated_reasons.description: Why each excluded method was excluded. A greyed name teaches nothing; the reason is what a practitioner learns from.

MethodModel.title: MethodModel
MethodModel.description: A registry entry, which is what drives the method form in the browser.

OCRCellModel.title: OCRCellModel
OCRCellModel.description:
One cell OCR proposed, with how far it is to be trusted.

`text` rather than a number, because what the user must check is the
characters Tesseract saw. An empty cell is `null` in the row.

OCRTableModel.title: OCRTableModel
OCRTableModel.description:
A photographed table, proposed for confirmation and nothing more.

Deliberately not a `PreparedDataModel`: nothing here has been inspected,
validated or stored against the test. A misread digit yields a plausible fit
and a wrong transmissivity, so the numbers become readings only when the
user sends the corrected grid back through the ordinary text route.

PastedReadings.title: PastedReadings
PastedReadings.description:
Readings pasted from a spreadsheet rather than uploaded as a file.

The limit is generous because a long test is a long table: 20,000 readings
of "time,drawdown" is well under it, and the byte ceiling still applies
once encoded.

derivative_figure.title: Derivative Figure
derivative_figure.description: Plotly JSON for the derivative diagnostic

figure.title: Figure
figure.description: Plotly JSON for the fit diagnostic

RetrievedDocModel.title: RetrievedDocModel
RetrievedDocModel.description:
One passage an answer was built from.

`document` is what the paper is called, not what folder it was filed in: the
field used to carry "Custom_Confined Aquifer", which identifies nothing a
reader could go and look up. `url` is present only where a link can be
derived rather than guessed — most of the corpus is paywalled, and a citation
that says so is more use than one that implies a link and 404s.

recovery_clock.title: Recovery Clock
recovery_clock.description: Whether the time column counts from pump start or stop
